conventions.convention: Units and potential outcomes are fixed; probability comes only from the declared finite assignment law. Partial interference requires invariance under changes outside the focal group, including allowed assignments having probability zero.
Population strategy means weight groups equally, whereas the Horvitz–Thompson exposure mean weights individual units equally.

The first stage selects exactly C groups uniformly for ψ; conditional on all strategy labels, within-group fixed-count assignments are uniform and independent across groups. Both treatment arms are nonempty.
DE is control minus treatment under ψ; IE, TE and OE subtract the relevant ψ mean from the relevant φ mean.

Finite-population variances and covariances use denominator population size minus one; observed sample variances use sample size minus one. Across-strategy variance estimators require C and N−C at least two; the direct estimator additionally requires both within-group arms at least two.

Event-conditioned expectations are defined by normalized finite weighted sums only for positive-probability events. The partition averaging identity assumes every partition cell has positive probability.
Horvitz–Thompson unbiasedness requires outcome sufficiency at each target exposure and strictly positive marginal exposure probability for every included unit; exposure independence is unnecessary.

load_bearing.statement: N>1 groups have fixed sizes n_i≥2 and potential outcomes satisfying partial interference. Exactly C∈{1,…,N−1} groups receive ψ uniformly; conditional on strategy labels, groups independently receive uniform K_i^s-element treatment subsets, with 1≤K_i^s<n_i. Strategy targets average the specified within-group conditional or unconditional outcomes, then average groups equally; estimators use the fixed positive arm and strategy counts.
For fixed real lists of length n≥2 and a uniformly selected m-element subset A, 1≤m≤n, E[x̄_A]=x̄ and Cov(x̄_A,ȳ_A)=(1−m/n)S_xy/m. When m≥2, E[s_xy,A]=S_xy.

For a finite probability space and real X, E[X|B] is the normalized weighted sum on every positive-probability event B. For 0<P(A)<1, the two-cell function is a version given σ(A). For a finite positive-probability partition, E[X]=Σ_q P(A_q)E[X|A_q].

For N≥4 and 2≤C≤N−2, group-specific finite second-stage variables with fixed means a_i(s), variances v_i(s), and the stated conditional independence satisfy Var(μ̂_s)=(1−C_s/N)S_s²/C_s+Σ_i v_i(s)/(C_s N) and E[s_X,s²]=S_s²+Σ_i v_i(s)/N. The expected arm-wise variance sum for the strategy contrast equals its design variance plus S_ψ−φ²/N.

For a fixed finite population, finite assignment law, partial interference, exposure sufficiency at d, and π_ij(d)>0 for every unit, E_p[μ̂_HT(d)]=μ(d). Differences for two labels satisfying these conditions are also design-unbiased, without exposure independence.

Under the defined two-stage design, each observed group mean conditional on its strategy is unbiased for its corresponding group target; population strategy means and all four displayed strategy contrasts are unbiased. Stratified interference and additive effects are unnecessary.

Under the two-stage design, stratified interference and 2≤C≤N−2, with 2≤K_i^ψ≤n_i−2 additionally for the direct variance estimator, E[V̂_D(ψ)]−Var(DÊ(ψ))=N⁻²Σ_i S_iD²(ψ)/n_i. The corresponding indirect, total and overall biases are S_I²/N, S_T²/N and S_O²/N. Each correction is nonnegative, with the stated exact constancy conditions for equality.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite outcome weights, event probabilities and allowance for zero-weight outcomes.
Finite weighted-sum expectations throughout the sampling and design arguments.
Centered second-moment definitions used in all sampling variance calculations.
Counting fixed-size subsets and deriving marginal and pairwise inclusion probabilities.
Finite linear algebra, scaling, splitting and nonnegativity of sums.
Interchanging finite sums and splitting sums over partitions or diagonal/off-diagonal index sets.
Expectation of finite linear combinations without an independence assumption.
Integral characterization verified by the finite event-conditioning lemma; completeness is not required.
Connecting finite weighted sums to the integral characterization of conditional expectation.
Interpreting fixed-schedule strategy and exposure targets as parameter functions.
Interpreting observed assignment/outcome formulas as estimators with real target spaces.
Adding conditional second-stage variances across groups; finite variables satisfy square integrability.
Transferring conditional independence of group assignments to their observed group statistics.

concerns.concern: The Definition begins 'In the finite-population model of [[def-potential-outcomes-under-partial-interference]]' but never assumes partial interference before using Y_ij(z_i). The cited definition explicitly permits arbitrary dependence on the global assignment and makes this reduced notation well-defined only when partial interference holds. For two singleton groups with all assignments allowed and Y_11(z_11,z_21)=z_21, an own-group exposure map exists but Y_11(z_11) does not. Thus the outcome-sufficiency clause uses an undefined object on the stated domain. The downstream HT theorem explicitly supplies partial interference, so its proof is unaffected.

The Definition allows sufficiency 'on a set of labels', then says 'For each label in the image of f_ij this condition defines a unique value Y_ij(d)' and asserts the unrestricted observed consistency identity. Sufficiency restricted to selected labels does not establish either conclusion at other labels. Within one two-unit group, take all four assignments, f_1(z)=z_1 and Y_1(z)=(1−z_1)z_2. The map is sufficient at label 1, but label 0 has outcomes 0 and 1, so Y_1(0) is undefined and the unconditional consistency identity cannot be asserted. The source's global consistency formulation assumes global sufficiency: [Aronow–Samii, §4, Conditions 1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1305.6156v4).

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and def-finite-randomized-treatment-assignment-model against the consuming partial-interference and exposure definitions. The supplier fixes units and schedules, permits global assignment dependence and zero-probability allowed assignments, and supplies only assignment randomness. The consumer's partial-interference definition preserves these conventions and introduces group invariance as an additional restriction. No sharp-null validity result is imported into the mean or variance arguments. The exposure-definition domain concerns are recorded separately.
